name: Unknown BSC swap-bot contract lets anyone swap approved wallets without slippage limits
summary: Unverified contract 0x16d7c6f4, used by an operator's EOAs to trade for managed wallets, let any caller name a wallet in f8c03cc4: it pulled that wallet's approved tokens, sold them on PancakeSwap V3 with no minimum output and bought the same amount back for the caller. After moving the pools, the attacker ran it for 152 approved wallets.
notes: Direct, immutable runtime (immutables: owner 0x6d8bace1, router 0x13f4ea83); the unauthenticated, zero-minimum entry exists from deployment, approvals only set exposure and the owner's later calls only withdraw.

Gross debits of the 152 wallets named in the three attacker txs (dust returned not netted). TA is valued at the attacker's realised 282,180.03 USDT (its own sale moved TA's price; DefiLlama 0.102143), WBNB and USD1 at DefiLlama.

Normal use is operator EOAs calling f8c03cc4 for third-party wallets, so exploits are the calls from contracts: a scan of every bot-touching tx from deployment to block 55250000 finds only the attacker's three. The defect is established from traces; there is no verified source.
